newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SAUDI HAPPY FOR NOW WITH 8.0 MLN QUOTA - GULF SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: SAUDI HAPPY FOR NOW WITH 8.0 MLN QUOTA - GULF SOURCE.

text.p: Saudi Arabia is happy with its eight million barrel per day (bpd) OPEC output allocation for the remainder of this year but won't make any commitment either way beyond that, a Gulf source on Wednesday.
"We are not planning to go beyond eight million for the time being," the Gulf source said.
OPEC ministers this week say they expect to leave unchanged output quotas under a 25.03 million bpd ceiling for six months from the end of June.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil supplier, already controls nearly a third of OPEC output.
"We are adhering to our quota and we don't plan going beyond that for the future of the agreement," said the Gulf source.
Saudi Arabia's crude output capacity remained at 10.3 million bpd and had no plans now to increase. "We are sticking to 10.3," he said.
The Gulf source said Saudi Arabia was comfortable with a supply-demand balance which it expected to deliver higher prices later this year.
Saudi Oil Minister Ali Naimi said on Tuesday that, despite quota violations by some OPEC members, he saw oil markets able to handle 26.5-27 million bpd of OPEC output.
The Saudis are keen to see oil prices back on an upward track after a 30 percent drop in prices from six-year highs since the beginning of the year.
But in spite of the price slump a conservative Saudi budget plan remains soundly on track for the year, Gulf analysts say.
Saudi Arabia saw world oil demand rising some 2.5 million bpd this year with OPEC supplying an incremental 1.5 million, the Gulf source said.
Overall demand for OPEC crude would run at some 27 million bpd. That is in line with most estimates of current actual output from the 11-member producer group.
He said rising demand for OPEC oil over the next five years could match or exceed the million barrels daily of incremental demand on OPEC seen each year over the past decade.
